unit.why: An anecdote, quoted from Zohar Hai, in which R. Naftali of Ropshitz asks a companion to learn the Mezhibozh rabbi's opinion of him, and for half a year the rabbi will not say a word about anyone.

stories.start_quote: עוד בס׳ זוהר חי הנ"ל שם
stories.end_quote: והוא מצער לשכינה ופוגם בה עכ״ל
stories.summary_en: R. Naftali of Ropshitz asks the narrator's father-in-law, a close relative and study partner of the rabbi of Mezhibozh, to find out what the rabbi thinks of him; for half a year the rabbi will not say even a small word about anyone, showing his holiness of speech.

tags.why: The story's point is the tzaddik's holiness of speech.

quotes: מקדושת הדיבור של רבינו הנ"ל ממעזיבוז
הי' לו משקל של זהב ממש בפיו
tags.why: Guarding one's speech is the virtue illustrated.

quotes: כיון שנקראים יהודים אסור לדבר עליהם
tags.why: The text states the prohibition on speaking against Jews.

quotes: והי' לומד עמו ביחד גמרא ותוספות
tags.why: The father-in-law studied Talmud together with the rabbi.

quotes: אברהם מרדכי איך בעט דיך האב רחמנות
tags.why: Naftali of Ropshitz asks a fellow hasid to learn the rabbi's opinion of him.

quotes: שלא ירע בשום דיבור לבר ישראל
tags.why: The restraint may reflect self-effacement; borderline.
The tale is framed as told by the author's father-in-law.
The father-in-law is a relative of the rabbi.
